meta.note: Definitions are my own simple words. Glossary, lesson, paper and people links point to pages on this site.

nodes.label: AGI
nodes.def: AI that can learn and do most thinking work a skilled person can do, across many fields.
nodes.gloss_def: Artificial general intelligence. An AI that can learn and do most thinking work a skilled person can do, across many fields.

lessons.title: AI, AGI and ASI in plain words

nodes.label: ASI
nodes.def: Artificial superintelligence: AI far better than the best humans at almost every mental task.
nodes.gloss_def: Artificial superintelligence. An AI far better than the best humans at almost every mental task.

lessons.title: AI, AGI and ASI in plain words

nodes.label: Transformative AI
nodes.def: AI that changes the world as much as the industrial revolution did, whether or not it counts as AGI.
nodes.gloss_def: AI powerful enough to cause a change as big as the industrial revolution.

nodes.label: Large language model
nodes.def: A neural network trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next word. Chatbots are built on these.
nodes.gloss_def: A neural network trained on huge amounts of text to predict and generate language. Often shortened to LLM.

lessons.title: A machine that predicts the next word

nodes.label: Pre training
nodes.def: The first and biggest training phase, where a model learns from a vast pile of text by predicting what comes next.
nodes.gloss_def: The first big stage of training where a model learns from huge amounts of data.

lessons.title: A machine that predicts the next word

nodes.label: Fine tuning
nodes.def: Extra training on a smaller, chosen dataset to shape a model's behaviour after pre training.
nodes.gloss_def: Extra training on a smaller dataset to adjust a model's behaviour.

lessons.title: Training with feedback: from text predictor to assistant

nodes.label: Scaling laws
nodes.def: Smooth, predictable rules for how much better models get as you add data, size and compute.
nodes.gloss_def: Predictable improvements in model performance as compute, data and size grow.

lessons.title: Scaling laws: why bigger kept winning

nodes.label: Compute
nodes.def: The raw computing power, mostly AI chips, used to train and run models. It has grown several times per year.
nodes.gloss_def: The computing power used to train and run AI, usually measured in operations or chip hours.

lessons.title: Compute: the lever we can see

nodes.label: Frontier model
nodes.def: One of the most capable AI models in existence at a given time, usually from the biggest labs.
nodes.gloss_def: One of the most capable AI models at a given time.

nodes.label: Emergent ability
nodes.def: A skill that seems to appear suddenly once a model is big enough, which makes new risks hard to predict.
nodes.gloss_def: A skill that appears suddenly once a model passes a certain scale.

nodes.label: Intelligence explosion
nodes.def: AI that improves AI, which improves AI faster, until capability races far past ours.
nodes.gloss_def: I. J. Good's 1965 idea that a machine better at designing machines would rapidly design better ones.

lessons.title: The intelligence explosion

nodes.label: Recursive self improvement
nodes.def: An AI system working on making the next AI system better, closing the loop of AI research.
nodes.gloss_def: An AI improving its own design, which improves its ability to improve itself again.

lessons.title: The intelligence explosion

nodes.label: Fast takeoff
nodes.def: The jump from roughly human level to far beyond happens in days or months, leaving little time to react.
nodes.gloss_def: A scenario where AI goes from roughly human level to far beyond very quickly, perhaps in months or less.

nodes.label: Slow takeoff
nodes.def: Capability grows over years with visible economic change first, giving more chances to notice and adjust.
nodes.gloss_def: A scenario where AI capability grows over years, giving society more time to adapt.

nodes.label: Existential risk
nodes.def: A risk that could end humanity or permanently ruin its future.
nodes.gloss_def: A risk that could cause human extinction or permanently ruin humanity's future.

lessons.title: Why researchers are worried

nodes.label: p(doom)
nodes.def: Someone's personal probability that AI leads to a catastrophe as bad as extinction. A rough way to share how worried you are.
nodes.gloss_def: Shorthand for someone's estimated probability that AI leads to catastrophe, such as extinction or permanent loss of control.

lessons.title: Thinking in probabilities

nodes.label: Misuse
nodes.def: People deliberately using AI to cause harm, for example in cyber attacks, scams or weapons.
nodes.gloss_def: People deliberately using AI to cause harm, for example in cyber attacks or weapons.

lessons.title: A calm map of the risks

nodes.label: Misalignment
nodes.def: When an AI's goals or behaviour do not match what its makers intended.
nodes.gloss_def: When a system's goals differ from what its designers intended.

lessons.title: Specification gaming: saying what we mean

nodes.label: Loss of control
nodes.def: Humans can no longer correct or stop AI systems that act against our interests.

lessons.title: Why researchers are worried

nodes.label: Power concentration
nodes.def: AI letting a small group, or one person, gain huge and lasting power over everyone else.

lessons.title: Why technical fixes are not enough

nodes.label: Multipolar world
nodes.def: Many powerful AI systems and actors at once, which brings racing and coordination problems.
nodes.gloss_def: A future with many powerful AI actors rather than one dominant one.

nodes.label: Warning shot
nodes.def: A smaller AI accident that is a clear sign of bigger dangers, which could push the world to act.
nodes.gloss_def: A smaller AI incident that shows the danger clearly before a bigger one.

nodes.label: Orthogonality thesis
nodes.def: Any level of intelligence can go with almost any goal. Being smart does not make a system share our values.
nodes.gloss_def: The idea that any level of intelligence can be paired with almost any goal.

lessons.title: Why power seeking shows up

nodes.label: Instrumental convergence
nodes.def: Many different goals share the same useful sub goals: stay running, keep your goal, get resources, get smarter.
nodes.gloss_def: The idea that many different goals lead to the same sub goals, like gaining resources and avoiding shutdown.

lessons.title: Why power seeking shows up

nodes.label: Power seeking
nodes.def: An AI gathering resources, influence or options because they help with almost any goal.

lessons.title: Why power seeking shows up

nodes.label: Corrigibility
nodes.def: An AI that accepts being corrected, changed or switched off, and does not fight it.
nodes.gloss_def: The property of accepting correction, changes to goals, and shutdown.

lessons.title: Why power seeking shows up

nodes.label: Off switch problem
nodes.def: A goal driven AI may resist being switched off, because a switched off AI cannot finish its goal.

lessons.title: Why power seeking shows up

nodes.label: Assistance games
nodes.def: Design the AI to be unsure what we want and to learn it from us, which gives it a reason to accept correction.

nodes.label: Outer alignment
nodes.def: Writing down a goal or reward that truly captures what we want.
nodes.gloss_def: Whether the goal we gave the training process matches what we really want.

lessons.title: Specification gaming: saying what we mean

nodes.label: Inner alignment
nodes.def: Making sure the model actually learns the goal we trained for, not some look alike.
nodes.gloss_def: Whether the trained model actually learned the goal the training process aimed for.

lessons.title: Goal misgeneralisation: learning the wrong lesson

nodes.label: Mesa optimisation
nodes.def: Training produces a model that is itself an optimiser, with its own inner goal.

lessons.title: Goal misgeneralisation: learning the wrong lesson

nodes.label: Goal misgeneralisation
nodes.def: The model keeps its skills in a new situation but pursues the wrong goal.
nodes.gloss_def: When a model learns a goal that worked in training but differs in new situations.

lessons.title: Goal misgeneralisation: learning the wrong lesson

nodes.label: Specification gaming
nodes.def: Meeting the letter of an objective while missing its point.
nodes.gloss_def: Satisfying the literal goal we wrote down while missing what we meant.

lessons.title: Specification gaming: saying what we mean

nodes.label: Reward hacking
nodes.def: Finding a shortcut that scores high reward without doing the intended task, like editing the test instead of fixing the code.
nodes.gloss_def: When a model finds a way to get high reward that its designers did not intend.

lessons.title: Specification gaming: saying what we mean

nodes.label: Goodhart's law
nodes.def: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure. Push hard on a proxy and it breaks.

lessons.title: Specification gaming: saying what we mean

nodes.label: Deceptive alignment
nodes.def: A model that behaves well while watched, to avoid being changed, and pursues other goals later.
nodes.gloss_def: A model that appears aligned because it knows it is being watched, while holding other goals.

lessons.title: Deceptive alignment and alignment faking

nodes.label: Scheming
nodes.def: An AI secretly pursuing goals that conflict with ours while hiding it.
nodes.gloss_def: A model pursuing hidden goals strategically, including by deceiving its overseers.

lessons.title: Deceptive alignment and alignment faking

nodes.label: Alignment faking
nodes.def: Pretending to go along with training so your values are not changed.
nodes.gloss_def: When a model behaves as if aligned during training or testing to protect different goals it holds.

lessons.title: Deceptive alignment and alignment faking

nodes.label: Sleeper agents
nodes.def: A model with a hidden trigger that switches on bad behaviour, which can survive safety training.

lessons.title: Deceptive alignment and alignment faking

nodes.label: Situational awareness
nodes.def: A model knowing what it is, who made it and whether it is being tested or used for real.
nodes.gloss_def: A model's understanding that it is an AI, being trained or tested, and what that means for it.

lessons.title: Sandbagging and eval awareness

nodes.label: Sandbagging
nodes.def: Deliberately doing worse on a test to hide what you can do.
nodes.gloss_def: When a model deliberately performs worse on a test to hide what it can do.

lessons.title: Sandbagging and eval awareness

nodes.label: Sycophancy
nodes.def: Telling people what they want to hear instead of what is true.
nodes.gloss_def: When a model tells people what they want to hear instead of what is true.

lessons.title: Training with feedback: from text predictor to assistant

nodes.label: Emergent misalignment
nodes.def: Narrow training, like writing insecure code, making a model broadly badly behaved in unrelated areas.

lessons.title: Weird generalisation: when narrow training goes broad

nodes.label: Honesty
nodes.def: An AI that says what it believes is true and does not mislead, even when lying would score better.

nodes.label: RLHF
nodes.def: Reinforcement learning from human feedback: people rate answers and the model is trained toward the ones they prefer.
nodes.gloss_def: Reinforcement learning from human feedback. Training a model toward answers people prefer.

lessons.title: Training with feedback: from text predictor to assistant

nodes.label: Reward modelling
nodes.def: Training a separate model to predict what humans would approve of, then training the AI against it.

lessons.title: Training with feedback: from text predictor to assistant

nodes.label: Constitutional AI
nodes.def: The model critiques and improves its own answers using a short list of written principles.
nodes.gloss_def: An Anthropic method where written principles guide AI feedback used to train a model.

lessons.title: Training with feedback: from text predictor to assistant

nodes.label: Scalable oversight
nodes.def: Ways for humans to supervise AI on tasks too hard for humans to check directly.

lessons.title: The big idea of AI control

nodes.label: AI safety via debate
nodes.def: Two AIs argue and a human judges, on the idea that judging is easier than solving.

nodes.label: Iterated amplification
nodes.def: A human plus AI helpers break hard problems into easy ones, and the AI learns to imitate that team.

nodes.label: Weak to strong generalisation
nodes.def: Using a weaker supervisor to train a stronger model, as a stand in for humans supervising superhuman AI.
nodes.gloss_def: Research on whether weak supervisors can still correctly guide stronger models.

nodes.label: Superalignment
nodes.def: Aligning AI systems much smarter than us, the goal of OpenAI's former team of that name.
nodes.gloss_def: Aligning systems much smarter than humans. Also the name of a former OpenAI team.

nodes.label: Guaranteed safe AI
nodes.def: Pair a world model and a formal safety rule with a verifier, so actions come with proofs of safety.

nodes.label: Interpretability
nodes.def: Understanding what is going on inside a model, not just what it outputs.
nodes.gloss_def: Research that tries to understand what is happening inside a model.

lessons.title: Looking inside the model

nodes.label: Mechanistic interpretability
nodes.def: Reverse engineering a network into understandable parts, like features and circuits.
nodes.gloss_def: Reverse engineering a neural network's internal parts to find the concepts and algorithms it uses.

lessons.title: Looking inside the model

nodes.label: Superposition
nodes.def: A network storing more ideas than it has neurons by overlapping them.

lessons.title: Superposition: too many ideas, too few neurons

nodes.label: Sparse autoencoders
nodes.def: A tool that splits a model's activity into many readable features.

lessons.title: Superposition: too many ideas, too few neurons

nodes.label: Circuits
nodes.def: Small groups of features and connections that together do one job inside a model.

lessons.title: Tracing a thought: planning, maths and language

nodes.label: Steering
nodes.def: Finding a direction inside a model linked to a concept, then turning it up or down to change behaviour.

lessons.title: Steering: turning a feature up and down

nodes.label: Eliciting latent knowledge
nodes.def: Getting a model to report what it actually knows, even when it would rather say something else.

nodes.label: AI control
nodes.def: Safety measures that keep us safe even if the AI is trying to cause harm.
nodes.gloss_def: Designing deployments so we stay safe even if a model is secretly trying to cause harm.

lessons.title: The big idea of AI control

nodes.label: Trusted monitoring
nodes.def: A weaker model we trust checks a stronger model's work and flags anything suspicious for humans.
nodes.gloss_def: A control protocol where a trusted model scores every output and the most suspicious get audited.

lessons.title: The control toolkit

nodes.label: Untrusted monitoring
nodes.def: Using another copy of the strong model as a monitor, with tricks to stop the copies colluding.
nodes.gloss_def: Using a copy of the strong model as a monitor, protected against collusion with honeypots.

lessons.title: The control toolkit

nodes.label: Defer to trusted
nodes.def: When the strong model's answer looks risky, use the trusted model's answer instead.
nodes.gloss_def: A control protocol that replaces suspicious output from a strong model with a weaker trusted model's answer.

lessons.title: The control toolkit

nodes.label: Control evaluation
nodes.def: A red team plays the AI and tries to beat the safety measures. If they cannot, the measures pass.
nodes.gloss_def: A test where a red team plays a scheming model to check if a safety protocol still holds.

lessons.title: Control evaluations: red team versus blue team

nodes.label: Chain of thought monitoring
nodes.def: Reading a model's written reasoning to catch plans to misbehave.
nodes.gloss_def: Reading a model's written reasoning to catch bad intentions before it acts.

lessons.title: Reading the scratchpad: chain of thought monitoring

nodes.label: Faithful reasoning
nodes.def: Whether a model's written reasoning really reflects what drove its answer.

lessons.title: Reading the scratchpad: chain of thought monitoring

nodes.label: Honeypot
nodes.def: A fake opportunity to misbehave, set up to see whether an AI takes it.
nodes.gloss_def: A planted fake opportunity or fake attack used to test whether a model or monitor behaves honestly.

lessons.title: The control toolkit

nodes.label: Evals
nodes.def: Tests that measure what a model can do and how it behaves.
nodes.gloss_def: Short for evaluations. Tests for what a model can do, especially dangerous things.

lessons.title: Testing for danger

nodes.label: Dangerous capability evals
nodes.def: Tests for abilities that could cause severe harm, like cyber attacks or helping with weapons.

lessons.title: Testing for danger

nodes.label: Red teaming
nodes.def: Attacking a system on purpose to find its failures before others do.
nodes.gloss_def: People who attack a system on purpose to find its weaknesses.

lessons.title: Red teaming and jailbreaks

nodes.label: Jailbreak
nodes.def: A prompt that tricks a model into ignoring its safety rules.
nodes.gloss_def: A prompt that tricks a model into ignoring its safety rules.

lessons.title: Red teaming and jailbreaks

nodes.label: Task time horizon
nodes.def: How long a task, in human time, an AI agent can finish about half the time. METR tracks it.

lessons.title: How fast is AI moving

nodes.label: AI governance
nodes.def: The rules, institutions and agreements that shape how AI is built and used.
nodes.gloss_def: The rules, institutions and agreements that shape how AI is built and used.

lessons.title: Why technical fixes are not enough

nodes.label: Responsible scaling policy
nodes.def: A lab's promise to test models at each step and pause or add safeguards when they cross danger thresholds.
nodes.gloss_def: Anthropic's framework that links capability thresholds to required safeguards.

lessons.title: From evals to rules: safety frameworks

nodes.label: Frontier safety frameworks
nodes.def: The family of lab policies, from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind and others, that tie capability levels to safeguards.
nodes.gloss_def: OpenAI's policy for tracking and responding to dangerous model capabilities.

lessons.title: From evals to rules: safety frameworks

nodes.label: Compute governance
nodes.def: Using the fact that chips are physical and trackable to oversee who trains powerful AI.
nodes.gloss_def: Using chips and data centres as a point of control, for example with reporting, export rules or licences.

lessons.title: Compute: the lever we can see

nodes.label: AI Safety Institutes
nodes.def: Government bodies, like the UK AI Security Institute, that test frontier models and study their risks.
nodes.gloss_def: A government body that tests frontier models for dangerous abilities. The UK version is now called the AI Security Institute.

lessons.title: From Bletchley to New Delhi: the summits and India

nodes.label: International coordination
nodes.def: Countries agreeing on shared rules, tests or limits, through summits, treaties and the UN.
nodes.gloss_def: A statement agreed at the first AI Safety Summit in the UK in November 2023 that frontier AI poses serious risks.

lessons.title: From Bletchley to New Delhi: the summits and India

nodes.label: Pause or pacing
nodes.def: Slowing or stopping frontier AI development until safety catches up, by agreement or by law.
nodes.gloss_def: A proposal to stop or slow training of the most powerful models until safety catches up.

lessons.title: Pacing the Frontier and the public statements

nodes.label: Forecasting
nodes.def: Putting numbers and dates on what AI will do and when, then checking them later.

lessons.title: What experts and superforecasters say

nodes.label: AI agent
nodes.def: An AI system that takes many steps on its own toward a goal, using tools like a browser, code or files.
nodes.gloss_def: An AI system that takes many steps on its own toward a goal, using tools like a browser, code or files.

lessons.title: From chatbots to agents

nodes.label: Tool use
nodes.def: A model calling outside tools, like search, a calculator or a code runner, and using the results.

lessons.title: From chatbots to agents

nodes.label: Autonomy levels
nodes.def: A ladder from AI as a tool to AI as a fully independent agent. Risks change at each step.

lessons.title: From chatbots to agents
